descriptions.text: KipCoin announced that the attacker gained access to the server in 2014 and downloaded the wallet.dat file. A few months later, the attacker stole more than 3,000 BTC.

KipCoin, a Chinese Bitcoin exchange, was compromised after an attacker gained access to its wallet.dat file in May 2014. The hacker controlled exchange Bitcoin addresses and withdrew over 3,000 BTC in several transactions from October to December 2014. KipCoin disclosed the breach in February 2015 and shut down operations. No funds were recovered. The attacker accessed the exchange server and extracted the wallet.dat file, acquiring private keys needed to control KipCoin's Bitcoin wallets. The absence of timely wallet rotation, strong server security, and withdrawal controls enabled the theft.
